changes.reason: Add an analytic d shell on each atom (count 2×(4+5)=18 ≤ num_bands 27, checked with validate_deck). This gives the dispersive conduction band functions to live in, so the frozen window no longer forces long-range hoppings into an 8-function sp3 basis.

diagnosis: The construction fails only on the truncated-hopping test. Without truncation the model reproduces the path bands to 13.8 meV, but cutting every hopping longer than r_c = 9.99 Å raises the error to 52.3 meV. Even at E_F (ν=0) the truncated error is 26.6 meV, against 4.7 meV untruncated, and it peaks in the lowest conduction bands (DFT bands 10–11), which are 100–200 meV off at E_F+1–2 eV. The hoppings beyond r_c hold only 1.4e-4 of |H|² but still carry this error. The spreads are balanced (ratio 1.10), the centres sit on the bonds, and both minimisations converged. So this is not a gauge or optimiser problem. The cause is the 8-function sp3 basis: it has to carry the strongly dispersive GaAs conduction band, which is forced into the subspace by the frozen window at E_F+2.16 eV. A minimal sp3 basis can reproduce that band only with long-range hoppings. The frozen-window lever is already used up (PDWF at 1.2, 2.16 and 2.5 eV gave 102, 40 and 49 meV). Switching from atomic s/p to sp3 hybrids under SMV left the result essentially where it was (52 meV). The next lever is the projector set itself. Adding a d shell on each atom gives the conduction states, which have d character away from Γ, functions of their own. That enlarges the basis so the frozen conduction states can be represented with short-range hoppings. The Ga 3d semicore exclusion stays: that block is isolated 1.97 eV below and the gate honours the cut.
